title: kubestream — Drift by Actor
description: Who is changing the cluster, and how much of it your GitOps controller is not responsible for. Every panel here reads Modified rows grouped by the field-manager names in actors, with one variable naming the GitOps controller's manager so its changes can be told apart from everything else. The changes that remain are the drift: kubectl edits, mutating webhooks, other operators, and controllers reacting to them.

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: The ClickHouse holding kubestream's resource_states table.

list.name: cluster
list.label: Cluster
list.description: cluster_id is the leading column of the sort key, so every panel filters on it.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT cluster_id FROM resource_states ORDER BY cluster_id

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT cluster_id FROM resource_states ORDER BY cluster_id

list.name: namespace
list.label: Namespace
list.description: Multi-select. Leave on All to see the whole cluster; narrow it when one team's namespaces are the question.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT namespace FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY namespace

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT namespace FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY namespace

list.name: gitops_manager
list.label: GitOps manager name
list.description: The field-manager name your GitOps controller applies under, exactly as it appears in metadata.managedFields — Argo CD uses argocd-controller (older releases: argocd-application-controller), Flux uses the name of the applying kustomize-controller. Set it once and the exclusion panels become 'everything my GitOps controller did not do'. A name that matches nothing simply excludes nothing, so a wrong value shows up as a suspiciously high non-GitOps share rather than as an error.

panels.title: Share of changes the GitOps controller touched
panels.description: The percentage of Modified rows in the window whose actors include the GitOps manager name. A cluster reconciled entirely from Git sits near 100%; the gap below it is the drift the other panels break down. Note that a row is counted as GitOps-touched if the manager appears at all — a hand-edit to an object the controller also manages credits both, which is why this is a share rather than a verdict.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    round(100 * countIf(has(actors, ${gitops_manager:sqlstring})) / greatest(count(), 1), 1) AS gitops_share_pct
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
  AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)

panels.title: Objects with non-GitOps drift
panels.description: Distinct objects that were modified at least once in the window without the GitOps manager among the actors. This is the number to watch after a freeze or during an incident: it counts objects, not rows, so one object edited fifty times does not drown out fifty objects edited once.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    uniqExact((api_group, kind, namespace, name)) AS objects_with_drift
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
  AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND NOT has(actors, ${gitops_manager:sqlstring})

panels.title: Top actors, GitOps excluded
panels.description: The ranking that answers 'so who is it, then'. Each bar is one field-manager name and the number of Modified rows it appears on, with the GitOps manager filtered out. Expect controllers you did not think about — status writers, HPAs, and mutating webhooks all hold field ownership and all show up here.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    actor,
    count() AS modifications
FROM
(
    SELECT arrayJoin(actors) AS actor
    FROM resource_states FINAL
    WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
      AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
      AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
      AND $__timeFilter(ts)
)
WHERE actor != ${gitops_manager:sqlstring}
GROUP BY actor
ORDER BY modifications DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.title: Modified rows by actor over time
panels.description: The same grouping as the ranking, spread over time and including the GitOps manager so its reconcile cadence is visible as the baseline. Drift reads as a series that appears where the GitOps series is quiet — a burst of one manager's changes outside a deploy window is the thing to click into on the table below.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
    actor,
    count() AS modifications
FROM
(
    SELECT ts, arrayJoin(actors) AS actor
    FROM resource_states FINAL
    WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
      AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
      AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
      AND $__timeFilter(ts)
)
GROUP BY time, actor
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Objects changed without the GitOps controller
panels.description: The drift itself, one row per object: how often it changed, who changed it, and when it last moved. Copy an object's namespace, kind and name into the Object Timeline dashboard to see the individual diffs. An object whose only actor is a status writer is usually noise; an object with a human's kubectl manager on it is usually the finding.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    namespace,
    kind,
    name,
    count()  AS modifications,
    max(ts)  AS last_change,
    arrayStringConcat(arraySort(groupUniqArrayArray(actors)), ', ') AS field_managers
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
  AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND NOT has(actors, ${gitops_manager:sqlstring})
GROUP BY namespace, kind, name
ORDER BY modifications DESC
LIMIT 100
